purpose: A tiny deliberately-insecure demo notes web app (single Express server, 3 source files) used for security testing/training. Users sign in with username/password, then list, search, read, and create short text notes; data lives in an in-memory sql.js (WASM SQLite) database seeded with two test users.
authModel: Username/password login POST that sets a plaintext `user=<username>` cookie; the cookie alone identifies the current user on every request — no sessions, tokens, or hashing.
notableDirs: src/server.ts — all routes: home, /search, /login, /notes/:id, POST /notes, /go redirect
src/db.ts — in-memory DB bootstrap, seeded users/notes, query helpers
summary: A minimal Express + TypeScript notes web app, intentionally insecure, with all logic in three files under `src/`. State is an in-memory sql.js SQLite database seeded with two users and two notes; there are no external services. Authentication is a POST /login form that sets a plaintext `user` cookie, which is then trusted as the identity on every request. The highest-risk surface is `src/server.ts`, which handles all request routing, query-string and form input, cookie parsing, and redirects, with HTML rendered via string templates in `src/views.ts` and all data access in `src/db.ts`.
